circle.statement: Φ_t(z) = e^(iωt)z is a one-parameter group action of (ℝ, +) on S¹: Φ_0 = id, Φ_t∘Φ_s = Φ_(t+s); |γ_ω(t)| = 1 for every real t
for ω ≠ 0 the minimal positive period is T = 2π/|ω|
for ω ≠ 0, lim_(t→∞) cos ωt and sin ωt do not exist; both stay in [−1, 1]: the old wording "sines and cosines converge to infinity" is FALSE
t, the phase lift θ = ωt and the cycle count N(t) are unbounded; the image is the compact S¹, reached in one period
Stab(z) = Tℤ for every z (Stab = ℝ when ω = 0); the orbit map induces ℝ/Tℤ ≅ S¹, and with p(σ) = e^(2πiσ), γ_ω(t) = p(ωt/2π): ℝ/Tℤ ≅ ℝ/ℤ ≅ S¹ by t ↦ ωt/2π (T ↦ ±1)

p: ℝ → S¹ is a covering map (fibres σ + ℤ, deck translations, local diffeomorphism); the lift of γ_ω is σ(t) = ωt/2π. The unbounded object is the covering coordinate; S¹ is compact and is not called infinite

circleNote: The acting parameter is ℝ; the orbit/image geometry is S¹. The finite/infinite relation is exact: an unbounded covering parameter represents a compact periodic geometry because points separated by the period are identified (the quotient ℝ/Tℤ). Nothing about the circle converges.

torus.statement: (e^(iω_1t), …, e^(iω_nt)) is periodic ⟺ ∃T > 0 with Tω_j ∈ 2πℤ for all j ⟺ (for ω ≠ 0) all ratios ω_j/ω_k are rational (commensurable); minimal period T/2π = lcm(b_j)/gcd(a_j) for ω_j = a_j/b_j > 0
(1, √2): Stab = {0} at every point (the orbit map ℝ → T² is injective); the orbit is dense in T² (Kronecker; checked: 400 section returns come within 0.016 of every grid point)
torus.status: PROVED (stabilizer); density: known theorem, source-locked, numerical instance carded

torus.status: PROVED for the examples; the general statement is the Kronecker–Weyl theorem (source-locked)

cylinder.statement: Φ_t(z, x) = (e^(iωt)z, x + vt) on S¹ × ℝ, v ≠ 0: the angular projection is periodic (period 2π/|ω|); the full state has Stab = {0}; x(t) is unbounded; the orbit leaves every compact set (not recurrent)
a periodic state makes every observable periodic; a periodic observable (Re z) does not make the state periodic (x(t + T) − x(t) = 2πv/ω ≠ 0)

cylinderNote: One unbounded parameter drives a bounded periodic projection and an unbounded coordinate at the same time. Periodicity of a representation/projection is a different property from periodicity of the full state.

definitions: one-parameter action: a continuous map Φ: ℝ × X → X on a Hausdorff (here metric) space X with Φ_0 = id and Φ_t∘Φ_s = Φ_(t+s)
orbit: O(x) = {Φ_t(x) : t ∈ ℝ}; forward orbit: t ≥ 0
stabilizer: Stab(x) = {t ∈ ℝ : Φ_t(x) = x}, a subgroup of ℝ; it is closed because it is the preimage of the point x under the continuous map t ↦ Φ_t(x) into a Hausdorff space
framework.theorem: Stab(x) ∈ {ℝ, Tℤ (T > 0), {0}}. Proof: a closed subgroup H ≠ {0} has τ = inf(H ∩ (0, ∞)); if τ = 0, H contains arbitrarily small positive elements, so it is dense and, being closed, H = ℝ; if τ > 0, τ ∈ H (closed) and every h ∈ H lies in τℤ (division with remainder). The dense subgroup ℤ + √2ℤ is not closed and is never a stabilizer (A8Pa).

classes.name: periodic
classes.condition: Stab(x) = Tℤ; T is the minimal period and the orbit is homeomorphic to ℝ/Tℤ ≅ S¹ (continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space)
classes.example: circle, rational torus, rotation of ℝ²

classes.name: free, compact orbit closure, recurrent ("aperiodic recurrent"; quasi-periodic is the torus-linear-flow example of it)
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; forward orbit closure compact; Φ_(t_n)(x) → x for some t_n → ∞

classes.name: free, compact orbit closure, not recurrent
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; closure compact; no return near x
classes.example: logistic orbit converging to fixed points; θ̇ = 1 − cos θ on S¹

classes.name: free, drift
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; the forward orbit leaves every compact subset of X
classes.example: cylinder, translation on ℝ, the velocity flow on (−1, 1) (boundary approach)

classes.name: free, noncompact closure, not escaping
classes.condition: Stab(x) = {0}; closure noncompact but the orbit returns to some compact set for arbitrarily large t
classes.example: none carded in this pass; kept as a class

framework.exhaustive: The stabilizer trichotomy is logically exhaustive (theorem above). The sub-classes of free orbits come from two dichotomies (orbit closure compact or not; recurrent or not, resp. escaping or not), so the six classes are exhaustive as a decision tree; the named examples are known examples, not an exhaustive classification for this project.
terminology: "periodic" only for Stab = Tℤ (or fixed points when stated); an irrational torus flow is never called periodic
"quasi-periodic" only for linear flows on tori with rationally independent frequencies (or functions of such flows), not for every bounded non-periodic orbit
"recurrent" = positively recurrent (x lies in its own ω-limit set); near return ≠ exact return
"drift" = escapes every compact set; "boundary approach" is drift in an open state space that converges in an ambient space (A8Pg)
Poincaré recurrence is a measure statement: invariant measure, finite total measure, almost every point (A8Pd); it is not implied by compactness alone
framework.explains: It explains which behaviour occurs from objects the system supplies: the stabilizer (from the action), the orbit closure and recurrence (from the action and the topology of X). Unboundedness of the parameter is common to every row of the distinction table and decides nothing (A8Da).

star.name: forced periodicity
star.words: A constrained geometry forces every admissible evolution to be periodic.
star.verdict: FAIL. Compact T² with preserved invariants |z₁| = |z₂| = 1 and the (1, √2) flow has no periodic orbit at all (A8X1); compact [0, 1] with the logistic flow has no periodic non-fixed orbit (A8X3). Rejected: compact geometry ⇒ periodicity (A8Ra).

star.name: existence
star.words: A constrained geometry admits at least one periodic evolution.
star.verdict: RESTRICTED, in an explicitly defined category. Category: smooth manifolds without boundary (Hausdorff, second countable); admissible dynamics: flows of smooth complete vector fields. Statement: such a manifold carries a flow with a non-constant periodic orbit ⟺ some component has dimension ≥ 2 or is diffeomorphic to S¹. ⇐: a compactly supported bump-rotation field in a chart (A8Ba; compact support gives completeness, Lee 2013), or rotation of S¹. ⇒: otherwise every component is a point or ℝ (classification of 1-manifolds, Milnor 1965) and a flow on ℝ has no non-constant periodic orbit (A8Pe). If fixed points count as periodic, the claim is vacuous (Φ_t = id). Not stated for arbitrary "geometrical objects".

star.name: recurrence
star.words: Compact/constrained geometry tends to produce recurrence or near return.
star.verdict: RESTRICTED to the Poincaré recurrence theorem (known; PROVED under its hypotheses): for a measure-preserving flow on a space of finite total measure, almost every point is recurrent. These are the hypotheses of the standard theorem — of its guarantee — not necessary conditions for recurrence: the rotation of ℝ² (infinite measure) and θ̇ = 2 + cos θ on S¹ (Lebesgue not invariant; invariant density 1/(2 + cos θ)) recur everywhere (A8Va). In A8Pd's examples (cylinder: μ = ∞; logistic: Lebesgue not invariant; θ̇ = 1 − cos θ: only δ₀ invariant) the guarantee is unavailable and recurrence in fact fails there. Topological recurrence (some recurrent point on a compact metric space: minimal sets, Birkhoff) is a separate, weaker statement, source-only here.
